subject: redPanda
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: red panda balancing on a mossy stone.
Style: Genshin Impact.
reasoning:
Checking the render against red panda identity cues - the ears, face markings, and ringed tail look right, but the tail reads too dark red-brown instead of orange, the legs are too plum-colored and thin, and I'm noting the scarf as a problem area to fix next.

The scarf's ribbon tails are shooting upward like horns because the knot is placed at the top-back of the collar rather than draping naturally. I need to reposition the knot to the chest front or have the ribbons drape backward along the body surface instead of curving up into the air.

Adding gold bands along the sweep and a tassel spike at the trailing end, pointing back from the path's endpoint. Keeping the knot anchored at the top of the collar, and leaving the loose octahedron motes for atmosphere before moving on to the tail.

The tail's dark appearance is from the cel shading threshold facing away from light, so I'm shifting it to a darker red-brown on the back side, increasing ring contrast with a deep rust against orange instead of weak orange-on-orange, and adjusting the shadow tone to be less flat.

Also I realize the tail rising straight up hides behind the head in front view, so I'm angling it sideways with an S-curve offset so it's visible beside the head while still working as a counterbalance from the top.

The forehead tufts currently look like three odd orange spikes, so I want to shrink them and tilt their direction so they lie back closer to the head instead of jutting straight up.

I'll scrap that and sweep the tufts backward instead, laying them flat on top of the head like a crest rather than sticking up over the forehead.

For the face, the orange cap with cream around the eyes and muzzle looks right for a red panda. The cheek ruffs read a bit too spiky and beige—I should make them cream-white and slightly softer.

Checking the eyes, they look fine for size and placement from the front angle. For the body, the dark plum belly shading reads too heavy and black on the legs, so I want to lighten the dark tone to a less saturated plum-brown, and widen the leg radii since they look too thin and straight right now.

The panda stands on moss atop a wide stone, but the moss blobs at the rim are too big and clustered, hiding the paws — I'll shrink their size and reduce the count to clean up that area while keeping the overall platform proportions.

Resizing the base platform to better match the panda's footprint would require repositioning many connected elements like the props and ring textures, so I'll skip that larger change and focus on the smaller fixes. The teal collar ring reads fine in the front view as a hexagonal bib outline framing the chest.

I'm checking other details now — the hip gem visible in the three-quarter view, the cheek tuft near the jaw, and the head-to-body neck proportions all look acceptable. I'll move forward with editing the scarf ribbon code block.

Writing the ribbon sweep code...

Checking the body profile at that height and depth confirms this placement works with a slight lift and tapered sweep radius. I'll rig it to the chest bone for rigidity, even though hips might be closer for the rear portion.

Applying the drape with a small lift to the ribbon curve, I'm now worried about overlap with the belt — the belt sits lower with its own radius, and the ribbon's end point at roughly z=-0.005 to -0.09 risks crossing into the belt's z-range around -0.02. I should trim the ribbon's endpoint earlier so it terminates before reaching the belt region.

I'll end the ribbon at roughly z=0.045, just in front of the belt. Rather than a tassel spike, which would poke into the body, I'll cap it with a small gold bead sphere instead. Now I'm adjusting remaining details — tail points, dark coloring, leg radii, tufts, and moss counts, tweaking the moss loop and size variables so they're distinct from similar lines elsewhere.

I'm scaling up the leg radii for the forelegs and hind legs to give them more taper and bulk, and adjusting the paw width slightly. For the forehead tuft, I'm replacing the blade orientation so it lies flat against the head, using the direction and a sideways up vector to keep the leaf shape oriented correctly.

For the tail paint, I'm defining two color zones - most of the tail alternates between rust and orange stripes, but the tip switches to a dark brownish color. I'm also tweaking the dark color value and refining the ring colors to create more contrast between lit and shadowed stripes, plus a distinct tip color.
